title: Quote over footage
premise: The words are the content and the footage is the backdrop. The one blueprint that works when the shots are ordinary but the light is good.

copy.cta: Send this to who needs it

shots.what: Your calmest, best-lit frame. Nothing happening in it.
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Beautiful and empty. The text is the subject, so the shot must be quiet enough to read over — busy footage kills this format.

shots.what: A slow-moving frame — water, cloud, traffic, steam
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Something that moves slightly but goes nowhere. Motion holds the eye; movement across frame competes with the words.

shots.what: A human moment, small in the frame
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Put yourself in a corner of the frame and leave the middle empty for the text.

shots.what: A texture or detail with shallow depth
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Blur the background hard. Out-of-focus backdrops are the easiest place to put white text.

shots.what: The best light you have — sun through something, golden hour, a window
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: The last line lands here, so the shot has to lift. Shoot toward the light with something solid in front of it.

shots.what: Back to the opening frame — the loop
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Match shot 1 exactly. On a quote reel the loop matters more than anywhere else — people re-read.
